sentences.en: Scientists believe that a majority of the earth's bird population migrate in some fashion or other.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，地球上大多数鸟类种群均以某种方式迁徙。

sentences.en: Some travel seasonally for relatively short distances, such as birds that move from their winter habitats in lowlands to mountain tops for the summers.
sentences.zh: 有些鸟类季节性地进行相对较短距离的迁徙，例如冬季栖息于低地、夏季则飞往山顶的鸟类。

sentences.en: Others, like the Arctic Tern, travel more than 25,000 miles seasonally between the northern and southern poles.
sentences.zh: 而另一些鸟类，如北极燕鸥，则每年在北极与南极之间往返迁徙超过25,000英里。

sentences.en: Bird migration has been studied over many centuries through a variety of observations.
sentences.zh: 数个世纪以来，人们通过多种观察方式研究鸟类迁徙。

sentences.en: But until relatively recently, where birds went to in the winter was considered something of a mystery.
sentences.zh: 但直到相对近期，鸟类冬季去向仍被视为某种谜团。

sentences.en: The lack of modern science and technology led to many theories that we now recognize as error-filled and even somewhat amusing.
sentences.zh: 现代科学与技术的缺乏导致了许多如今被我们认定为充满谬误、甚至略显滑稽的理论。

sentences.en: Take hibernation theory for example – two thousand years ago, it was commonly believed that when birds left an area, they went underwater to hibernate in the seas and oceans.
sentences.zh: 以冬眠理论为例——两千年前，人们普遍相信鸟类离开某地后会潜入水下，在海洋中冬眠。

sentences.en: Another theory for the regular appearance and disappearance of birds was that they spent winter hidden in mud till the weather changed and food became abundant again.
sentences.zh: 另一种解释鸟类周期性出现与消失的理论认为：它们冬季藏身于泥中，待天气转暖、食物再度丰足时才现身。

sentences.en: The theory that some birds hibernate persisted until experiments were done on caged birds in the 1940s which demonstrated that birds have no hibernation instinct.
sentences.zh: 部分鸟类会冬眠的理论一直延续至20世纪40年代，直到人们在笼养鸟类身上开展实验，证实鸟类根本不具备冬眠本能，该理论才被推翻。

sentences.en: One of the earliest naturalists and philosophers from ancient Greece was Aristotle who was the first writer to discuss the disappearance and reappearance of some bird species at certain times of year.
sentences.zh: 古希腊最早的自然学家与哲学家之一亚里士多德，是首位撰文探讨某些鸟类物种在一年中特定时节消失又重现现象的作家。

sentences.en: He developed the theory of transmutation, the seasonal change of one species into another, by observing redstarts and robins.
sentences.zh: 他通过观察红尾鸲与知更鸟，提出了‘转化论’——即一种鸟类随季节变化而转变为另一种物种。

sentences.en: He observed that in the autumn, small birds called ‘redstarts' began to lose their feathers , which convinced Aristotle that they changed into robins for the winter, and back into redstarts in the summer.
sentences.zh: 他观察到秋季时一种名为‘红尾鸲’的小型鸟类开始脱落羽毛，由此确信它们冬季变为知更鸟，夏季再变回红尾鸲。

sentences.en: These assumptions are understandable given that this pair of species are similar in shape, but are a classic example of an incorrect interpretation based on correct observations.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这两种鸟类外形相似，这些假设不难理解；但它们恰恰是‘基于正确观察却得出错误结论’的经典范例。

sentences.en: The most bizarre theory was put forward by an English amateur scientist, Charles Morton, in the seventeenth century.
sentences.zh: 最离奇的理论由17世纪一位英国业余科学家查尔斯·莫顿提出。

sentences.en: He wrote a surprisingly well-regarded paper claiming that birds migrate to the moon and back every year.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了一篇出人意料地广受推崇的论文，声称鸟类每年往返月球一次。

sentences.en: He came to this conclusion as the only logical explanation for the total disappearance of some species.
sentences.zh: 他得出这一结论，是因为这是当时唯一能逻辑自洽地解释某些鸟类彻底消失现象的假说。

sentences.en: One of the key moments in the development of migration theory came in 1822 when a white stork was shot in Germany.
sentences.zh: 鸟类迁徙理论发展史上的一个关键节点出现在1822年，当时一只白鹳在德国被射杀。

sentences.en: This particular stork made history because of the long spear in its neck which incredibly had not killed it – everyone immediately realised this spear was definitely not European.
sentences.zh: 这只白鹳载入史册，是因为其颈部插着一支长矛——令人难以置信的是，它竟未因此丧命；人们立刻意识到这支长矛绝非欧洲制造。

sentences.en: It turned out to be a spear from a tribe in Central Africa.
sentences.zh: 后来证实，这支长矛源自中非某部落。

sentences.en: This was a truly defining moment in the history of ornithology because it was the first evidence that storks spend their winters in sub-Saharan Africa .
sentences.zh: 这确实是鸟类学史上具有里程碑意义的时刻，因为这是首次确凿证明白鹳冬季栖息于撒哈拉以南非洲的证据。

sentences.en: You can still see the ‘arrow stork' in the Zoological Collection of the University of Rostock in Germany.
sentences.zh: 如今，人们仍可在德国罗斯托克大学动物学收藏馆中看到这只‘带箭白鹳’。

sentences.en: People gradually became aware that European birds moved south in autumn and north in summer but didn't know much about it until the practice of catching birds and putting rings on their legs became established.
sentences.zh: 人们逐渐意识到欧洲鸟类秋季南迁、春季北返，但对此知之甚少，直至‘捕鸟环志’（即捕捉鸟类并在其腿部套上金属环）的做法得以普及。

sentences.en: Before this, very little information was available about the actual destinations of particular species and how they travelled there.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，关于特定鸟类实际目的地及其迁徙路径的信息极为匮乏。

sentences.en: People speculated that larger birds provided a kind of taxi service for smaller birds by carrying them on their backs.
sentences.zh: 人们曾推测大型鸟类会充当小型鸟类的‘空中出租车’，驮着它们飞行。

sentences.en: This idea came about because it seemed impossible that small birds weighing only a few grams could fly over vast oceans .
sentences.zh: 这种想法源于一个看似合理的困惑：仅重几克的小型鸟类似乎不可能飞越浩瀚大洋。

sentences.en: This idea was supported by observations of bird behaviour such as the harassment of larger birds by smaller birds.
sentences.zh: 该观点还得到一些鸟类行为观察的支持，例如小型鸟类骚扰大型鸟类的现象。

sentences.en: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 Audioscripts The development of bird ringing, by a Danish schoolteacher, Hans Christian Cornelius Mortensen, made many discoveries possible.
sentences.zh: 更多雅思干货，添加教主微信：519690129 听力原文：丹麦教师汉斯·克里斯蒂安·科尼利厄斯·莫滕森开创的鸟类环志法，使诸多发现成为可能。

sentences.en: This is still common practice today and relies upon what is known as ‘recovery' – this is when ringed birds are found dead in the place they have migrated to, and identified.
sentences.zh: 这一方法至今仍被广泛采用，其核心在于所谓‘回收’——即环志鸟在其迁徙目的地死亡后被发现并识别。

sentences.en: Huge amounts of data were gathered in the early part of the twentieth century and for the first time in history people understood where birds actually went to in winter.
sentences.zh: 20世纪早期积累了海量数据，人类历史上首次真正弄清了鸟类冬季的实际去向。

sentences.en: In 1931, an atlas was published showing where the most common species of European birds migrated to.
sentences.zh: 1931年，一本图集出版，标示出欧洲最常见鸟类的越冬地点。

sentences.zh: 关于鸟类迁徙的更新近理论……
